Service deskTicket workflow

Kopere Helpdesk

Bring support requests into Moodle so the ticket, user, course context, conversation and operational history stay in the same environment.

Users can open and follow tickets while support teams organize work by category, status and priority, add attachments, search conversations and retain searchable ticket conversations and reply history.

Operational workflow
  • Category-based support teams and routing.
  • Email notifications for new tickets and replies.
  • Ticket history for status, priority and category changes.
  • Scheduled reminders for unanswered requests.
  • Automatic closing of resolved tickets after the workflow period.
  • Optional read-only access to all tickets for authorized support staff.
Kopere Dashboard
local_kopere_dashboard provides the administrative foundation used by the plugin.
Kopere BI
local_kopere_bi provides the reporting layer for ticket demand, categories, service time and support activity.
AI-assisted features
AI-assisted features also require AI Bridge.
Built for support teams, not only ticket storage

The Helpdesk combines ticket management, conversation history, reporting and scheduled follow-up so pending work can be identified and acted on instead of disappearing into email threads or external systems.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

A support desk needs more than a ticket form: staff need to see who owns a request, what happened previously, which replies were sent and which issues still need attention. Helpdesk keeps that workflow close to the user's Moodle account and course context, while ticket history and category routing help teams respond consistently. Reminders and reports can help identify bottlenecks, but departments should establish clear ownership and response expectations. AI-assisted drafting, where enabled, remains subject to human review and its separately stated dependency.
